unitTag: Unit 1 • Numbers & Operations in Base Ten
title: Place Value, Powers of 10 & Product Estimation
subtitle: Master multidigit place value through millions, base-10 shifts (10 times more/less), multiplying by powers of 10, exponential notation, and strategic product estimation using rounding and compatible numbers.
stageBadge: Grade 5 • Place Value, Powers of 10 & Estimation

preStudy.title: Pre-Study: Check Your Readiness
preStudy.subtitle: Review essential prerequisite concepts: reading multi-digit whole numbers, multiplying by 10, and basic rounding before advancing to millions and powers of 10.

cards.title: 1. Understanding Periods & Digits
cards.desc:
Numbers are grouped into 3-digit periods separated by commas (Millions, Thousands, Ones):
• In each period, place values follow the repeating pattern: Hundreds, Tens, Ones.
• Example: In $213,560,447$, the digit 2 is in the hundred millions place.

cards.title: 2. The Base-Ten Shift Rule
cards.desc:
Our number system is based on ten:
• Moving 1 place to the left multiplies a digit's value by $10$ ($10\times$ more).
• Moving 1 place to the right divides a digit's value by $10$ ($10\times$ less).

cards.title: 3. What is an Exponent?
cards.desc:
Repeated multiplication can be written in exponential form:
$$10 \times 10 \times 10 = 10^3$$• Base: The repeated factor ($10$).
• Exponent: How many times the factor is repeated ($3$).

diagnosticQuestions.text: 1. In the number $421,389$, what is the place value of the digit 2?
diagnosticQuestions.explanation: The digit 4 is in hundred-thousands, 2 is in ten-thousands, and 1 is in thousands.

diagnosticQuestions.text: 2. What is the value of $10^4$ in standard form?
3. What is the estimated product of $69 \times 63$ using rounding to the nearest ten?

foundationRules.title: Place Value Structure & Three-Digit Periods
foundationRules.summary: Every whole number is partitioned into groups of three digits called periods (Ones, Thousands, Millions, Billions). Inside each period, the digits represent Hundreds, Tens, and Ones. A digit in one place has $10$ times the value of the same digit in the place to its right.
foundationRules.visualHtml:
213, 560, 447
Millions   |   Thousands   |   Ones

foundationRules.title: The 10-Times Principle (Left ×10, Right ÷10)
foundationRules.summary: When a digit shifts one place to the left, its value becomes $10$ times greater. When a digit shifts two places to the left, its value becomes $10 \times 10 = 100$ times greater. Conversely, shifting to the right divides its value by $10$ ($\\frac{1}{10}$ of its previous value).
foundationRules.visualHtml: 500 is $10\times$ more than 50, and $100\times$ more than 5.

foundationRules.title: Powers of 10 and Scientific Exponents
foundationRules.summary: An exponent indicates how many times the base ($10$) is multiplied by itself. For any whole number multiplied by $10^n$, write the number and append $n$ zeros: $$a \times 10^n = a\underbrace{00\dots0}_{n \text{ zeros}}$$Critical Rule: $10^3 = 1,000$ (NOT $30$). Never multiply the base by the exponent!
foundationRules.visualHtml: Common Trap: $10^3 \ne 30$ ($10 \times 3$). Correct: $10^3 = 10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1,000$.

foundationRules.title: Product Estimation: Rounding vs. Compatible Numbers
foundationRules.formula: $$\text{Rounding: Highest Place Value} \quad \text{vs.} \quad \text{Compatible: Mental Math Friendly}$$
foundationRules.summary:
Rounding Method: Round each factor to its greatest place value (e.g., $482 \times 19 \to 500 \times 20 = 10,000$).
Compatible Numbers Method: Substitute numbers with values close to the factors that make mental multiplication effortless (e.g., $225 \times 16 \to 250 \times 16 = 4,000$).
foundationRules.visualHtml: $69 \times 63 \approx 70 \times 60 = 4,200$ (Close to actual: $4,347$)

specialCases.title: The Zero Trap in Exponential Multiplication
specialCases.desc:
When multiplying a number that already ends in zeros by a power of 10, count the original zeros PLUS the exponent's zeros:
$$40 \times 10^3 = (4 \times 10^1) \times 10^3 = 4 \times 10^4 = 40,000$$
Do not stop at 3 zeros! The product has 4 zeros total ($1$ original $+ 3$ from $10^3$).

specialCases.title: Choosing Between Rounding and Compatible Numbers
specialCases.desc:
• Use Rounding when asked for standard algorithmic estimation or when numbers are naturally close to multiples of 10 or 100.
• Use Compatible Numbers when factors involve friendly fractions (like $25, 50, 75, 250$) or when factors easily multiply mentally ($25 \times 4 = 100$, $125 \times 8 = 1,000$).

ideas.title: Understanding Place Value & Multi-Digit Representation
ideas.flashcardTitle: Idea 1: Place Value through Millions & Number Forms
ideas.coreRule: Whole numbers are written in standard form ($213,560,447$), word form, and expanded form ($200,000,000 + 10,000,000 + \dots$). Each period has Hundreds, Tens, and Ones.

cards.badge: Solved Example 1.1 • Identifying Place Value & Value of Digits
cards.prompt:
Consider the multi-digit whole number $213,560,447$:
(a) State the place value and value of the digit $1$.
(b) State the place value and value of the digit $5$.
cards.solution:
Step 1
Identify the period and position of digit $1$: It is in the millions period, in the ten-millions place. Its value is $10,000,000$.
Step 2
Identify the period and position of digit $5$: It is in the thousands period, in the hundred-thousands place. Its value is $500,000$.
(a) Ten Millions, Value = $10,000,000$  |  (b) Hundred Thousands, Value = $500,000$

cards.badge: Solved Example 1.2 • Converting Standard Form to Expanded Form
cards.prompt:
Write each number in expanded form:
(a) $7,564,209$
(b) $1,000,000 + 300,000 + 40,000 + 500 + 60 + 2$ (write in standard form)
cards.solution:
Step 1
Decompose $7,564,209$ by the value of each digit:$$7,000,000 + 500,000 + 60,000 + 4,000 + 200 + 9$$ (Notice zero in the tens place contributes nothing).
Step 2
Combine the expanded values for (b): Align by place value: $1$ million, $3$ hundred-thousands, $4$ ten-thousands, $0$ thousands, $5$ hundreds, $6$ tens, $2$ ones $= 1,340,562$.
(a) $7,000,000 + 500,000 + 60,000 + 4,000 + 200 + 9$  |  (b) $1,340,562$

cards.badge: Solved Example 1.3 • Word Form to Standard Form
cards.prompt:
Write in standard form:
"Thirty-four million, two hundred seven thousand, eight hundred fifteen"
cards.solution:
Step 1
Break into three periods: Millions period: $34$, Thousands period: $207$, Ones period: $815$.
Step 2
Place commas between periods: $34,207,815$.
$34,207,815$

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 1.1 • Place Value Analysis
cards.prompt:
In the number $582,360,194$:
(a) What is the place value of the digit $8$?
(b) What is the value of the digit $2$?
cards.solution:
Step 1
The digit 8 is in the ten millions place.
Step 2
The digit 2 is in the millions place, so its value is $2,000,000$.
(a) Ten Millions  |  (b) $2,000,000$

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 1.2 • Standard & Expanded Forms
cards.prompt: Write $90,405,620$ in expanded form using values of digits.
cards.solution:
Step 1
Determine values: $9 \to 90,000,000$, $4 \to 400,000$, $5 \to 5,000$, $6 \to 600$, $2 \to 20$.
Step 2
Write the sum: $90,000,000 + 400,000 + 5,000 + 600 + 20$.
$90,000,000 + 400,000 + 5,000 + 600 + 20$

ideas.title: The 10-Times Principle & Place Value Shifts
ideas.coreRule: Moving a digit one place to the left multiplies its value by $10$. Moving two places to the left multiplies its value by $100$. Shifting to the right divides its value by $10$ ($\\frac{1}{10}$).

cards.badge: Solved Example 2.1 • Comparing Same Digits in Different Positions
cards.prompt:
In the number $55,240$:
How does the value of the digit $5$ in the ten-thousands place compare to the value of the digit $5$ in the thousands place?
cards.solution:
Step 1
Value of the first $5$ (ten-thousands) $= 50,000$. Value of the second $5$ (thousands) $= 5,000$.
Step 2
Divide values: $50,000 \div 5,000 = 10$. The first 5 is $10$ times greater than the second 5.
The $5$ in ten-thousands is $10$ times the value of the $5$ in thousands ($50,000 = 10 \times 5,000$).

cards.badge: Solved Example 2.2 • Two-Place Value Shifts (100 Times)
cards.prompt:
In the number $4,400$:
Explain the relationship between the value of the digit $4$ in the thousands place and the value of $4$ in the tens place if the number was $4,040$.
cards.solution:
Step 1
Value of 4 in thousands place $= 4,000$. Value of 4 in tens place $= 40$.
Step 2
The thousands place is $2$ positions to the left of the tens place. Moving 2 positions to the left multiplies by $10 \times 10 = 100$.$$4,000 \div 40 = 100$$
The 4 in thousands is $100$ times the value of the 4 in tens ($4,000 = 100 \times 40$).

cards.badge: Solved Example 2.3 • Dividing Whole Numbers by 10, 100, 1,000
cards.prompt:
Find each quotient and explain how the digits shifted:
(a) $806,335,000 \div 1,000$
(b) $450,000 \div 10$
cards.solution:
Step 1
Dividing by $1,000$ shifts all digits $3$ places to the right (reducing by a factor of $1,000$): $806,335,000 \div 1,000 = 806,335$.
Step 2
Dividing by $10$ shifts all digits $1$ place to the right (reducing by a factor of $10$): $450,000 \div 10 = 45,000$.
(a) $806,335$  |  (b) $45,000$

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 2.1 • Comparing Identical Digits
cards.prompt: In the number $77,314$, how many times greater is the value of the $7$ in the ten-thousands place than the $7$ in the thousands place?
cards.solution:
Step 1
The ten-thousands digit has value $70,000$. The thousands digit has value $7,000$.
Step 2
$70,000 \div 7,000 = 10$. It is $10$ times greater.
$10$ times greater ($70,000 = 10 \times 7,000$).

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 2.2 • Base-Ten Rightward Shift
cards.prompt: A number has a digit with value $600$. If that digit moves one place to the right, what will its new value be?
cards.solution:
Step 1
Moving one place to the right divides the value by $10$.
Step 2
$600 \div 10 = 60$.
The new value is $60$.

ideas.title: Powers of 10 & Exponential Form
ideas.coreRule: An exponent represents repeated multiplication: $10^n = 10 \times 10 \dots (n \text{ times})$. The exponent equals the number of zeros when written in standard form ($10^4 = 10,000$).

cards.badge: Solved Example 3.1 • Expressing Repeated Multiplication as Powers of 10
cards.prompt:
Write each product in exponential form and in standard form:
(a) $10 \times 10 \times 10$
(b) $10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10$
cards.solution:
Step 1
Count factors of 10 for (a): $10$ is multiplied $3$ times $\implies 10^3$. Standard form has 3 zeros: $1,000$.
Step 2
Count factors of 10 for (b): $10$ is multiplied $6$ times $\implies 10^6$. Standard form has 6 zeros: $1,000,000$.
(a) $10^3 = 1,000$  |  (b) $10^6 = 1,000,000$

cards.badge: Solved Example 3.2 • Evaluating Whole Numbers Multiplied by Powers of 10
cards.prompt:
Find the value of each expression:
(a) $7 \times 10^3$
(b) $9 \times 10^5$
cards.solution:
Step 1
Evaluate $10^3$: $10^3 = 1,000$. Then multiply: $7 \times 1,000 = 7,000$.
Step 2
Evaluate $10^5$: $10^5 = 100,000$. Then multiply: $9 \times 100,000 = 900,000$.
(a) $7,000$  |  (b) $900,000$

cards.badge: Solved Example 3.3 • Error Analysis in Exponents (Jonah, Zoey & Lamiaa)
cards.prompt:
Three students wrote their answers for $10^3$ and $10^4$:
• Jonah wrote: $10^3 = 30$
• Zoey wrote: $10^4 = 40$
• Lamiaa wrote: $10^3 = 100$
Explain the misconception each student made and provide the correct mathematical evaluation.
cards.solution:
Step 1
Jonah and Zoey multiplied the base by the exponent ($10 \times 3 = 30$ and $10 \times 4 = 40$). An exponent means repeated multiplication of the base, NOT multiplying base by exponent!
Step 2
Lamiaa only multiplied two tens ($10 \times 10 = 100 = 10^2$) instead of three tens ($10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1,000$).
Correct Values: $10^3 = 1,000$ and $10^4 = 10,000$.

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 3.1 • Scientific Powers of 10
cards.prompt: Write $10^5$ in standard form and in words.
cards.solution:
Step 1
$10^5 = 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 = 100,000$.
Step 2
In words: "One hundred thousand".
Standard: $100,000$  |  Word: One hundred thousand

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 3.2 • Exponent Error Analysis
cards.prompt: A student wrote $5 \times 10^2 = 50$. Explain the mistake and state the correct product.
cards.solution:
Step 1
The student calculated $5 \times (10 \times 1)$ or appended only 1 zero. But $10^2 = 100$.
Step 2
Correct product: $5 \times 100 = 500$.
The student used $10^1$ instead of $10^2$. Correct answer is $500$.

ideas.title: Multiplying Multi-Digit Numbers by Powers of 10
ideas.flashcardTitle: Idea 4: Multi-Digit Products with Powers of 10
ideas.coreRule: To multiply a multi-digit number by $10^n$, shift all digits $n$ places to the left, appending $n$ zeros to the right of the whole number.

cards.badge: Solved Example 4.1 • Mental Math Patterns with Powers of 10
cards.prompt:
Compute each product using mental math patterns:
(a) $52 \times 10^3$
(b) $145 \times 10^4$
cards.solution:
Step 1
For (a): The exponent is $3$. Append $3$ zeros to $52$: $52 \times 1,000 = 52,000$.
Step 2
For (b): The exponent is $4$. Append $4$ zeros to $145$: $145 \times 10,000 = 1,450,000$.
(a) $52,000$  |  (b) $1,450,000$

cards.badge: Solved Example 4.2 • Products Ending in Zero Multiplied by Powers of 10
cards.prompt:
Find the product: $30 \times 10^3$:
Explain why the product ends in four zeros rather than three.
cards.solution:
Step 1
Break $30$ into $3 \times 10^1$. Then:$$30 \times 10^3 = 3 \times 10^1 \times 10^3 = 3 \times 10^4$$
Step 2
$3 \times 10,000 = 30,000$. One zero came from the factor $30$ and three zeros came from $10^3$.
$30,000$ (Contains 4 zeros total).

cards.badge: Solved Example 4.3 • Real-World Spacecraft Mass Calculation
cards.prompt:
A space exploration probe has a mass of $3 \times 10^4\text{ kg}$.
Write the mass in standard form and determine how many 1,000 kg satellites would equal this probe's mass.
cards.solution:
Step 1
Standard form: $3 \times 10^4 = 3 \times 10,000 = 30,000\text{ kg}$.
Step 2
Divide by $1,000$: $30,000 \div 1,000 = 30$.
Standard mass = $30,000\text{ kg}$  |  Equals $30$ satellites of $1,000\text{ kg}$.

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 4.1 • Base-Ten Multiplication
cards.prompt: Find the product: $48 \times 10^4$.
cards.solution:
Step 1
$10^4 = 10,000$. Append 4 zeros to 48.
Step 2
$48 \times 10,000 = 480,000$.
$480,000$

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 4.2 • Missing Exponent
cards.prompt: Find the missing exponent $n$: $8 \times 10^n = 8,000,000$.
cards.solution:
Step 1
Count the zeros after the 8: There are 6 zeros.
Step 2
$8,000,000 = 8 \times 10^6$. Therefore, $n = 6$.
$n = 6$

ideas.title: Estimating Products Using Compatible Numbers & Rounding
ideas.coreRule: To estimate products, round each factor to its greatest place value or choose compatible numbers close to the actual values that make mental computation straightforward.

cards.badge: Solved Example 5.1 • Product Estimation via Rounding
cards.prompt:
Estimate each product by rounding to the nearest ten or hundred:
(a) $69 \times 63$
(b) $482 \times 19$
cards.solution:
Step 1
For (a): Round $69 \to 70$ and $63 \to 60$. Multiply: $70 \times 60 = 4,200$. (Actual $= 4,347$).
Step 2
For (b): Round $482 \to 500$ and $19 \to 20$. Multiply: $500 \times 20 = 10,000$. (Actual $= 9,158$).
(a) Estimate $= 4,200$  |  (b) Estimate $= 10,000$

cards.badge: Solved Example 5.2 • Product Estimation via Compatible Numbers
cards.prompt:
Estimate each product using compatible numbers:
(a) $9,358 \times 69$
(b) $225 \times 16$
cards.solution:
Step 1
For (a): Choose friendly numbers: $9,358 \to 9,000$ and $69 \to 70$. Mental math: $9 \times 7 = 63$, so $9,000 \times 70 = 630,000$.
Step 2
For (b): Notice $225 \approx 250$. Since $250 \times 4 = 1,000$ and $16 = 4 \times 4$: $250 \times 16 = 4,000$.
(a) Compatible Estimate $= 630,000$  |  (b) Compatible Estimate $= 4,000$

cards.badge: Solved Example 5.3 • Real-World Application: Airplane Distance & Furniture Cost
cards.prompt:
Solve both real-world estimation problems:
(a) An airplane flies at an average speed of $482$ miles per hour. Estimate how far it travels in $19$ hours.
(b) A company orders $41$ conference tables costing $\$85$ each. Estimate the total cost using rounding.
cards.solution:
Step 1
For airplane (a): Round speed $482 \to 500\text{ mph}$ and time $19 \to 20\text{ hours}$. Estimated distance $= 500 \times 20 = 10,000\text{ miles}$.
Step 2
For tables (b): Round $41 \to 40$ tables and $\$85 \to \$90$. Estimated cost $= 40 \times 90 = \$3,600$.
(a) Distance $\approx 10,000\text{ miles}$  |  (b) Cost $\approx \$3,600$

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 5.1 • Rounding Product Estimation
cards.prompt: Estimate the product of $78 \times 42$ by rounding each factor to the nearest ten.
cards.solution:
Step 1
Round $78 \to 80$ and $42 \to 40$.
Step 2
$80 \times 40 = 3,200$. (Actual $= 3,276$).
Estimated product is $3,200$.

cards.badge: Try-It Practice 5.2 • Compatible Numbers Strategy
cards.prompt: Use compatible numbers to estimate $492 \times 22$.
cards.solution:
Step 1
$492$ is close to $500$, and $22$ is close to $20$.
Step 2
$500 \times 20 = 10,000$.
Compatible estimate is $10,000$.

mcqs.question: In the number $213,560,447$, what is the place value of the digit 1?
mcqs.explanation: The digit 2 is in hundred-millions, 1 is in ten-millions, and 3 is in millions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following represents the number 7,564,209 in expanded form?
In the number 65,520, the 5 in the thousands place is how many times the value of the 5 in the hundreds place?
mcqs.explanation: The 5 in thousands has value 5,000, and the 5 in hundreds has value 500. Since 5,000 = 10 × 500, it is 10 times greater.

mcqs.question: What is the value of 806,335,000 ÷ 1,000?
mcqs.explanation: Dividing by 1,000 shifts the digits 3 places to the right (removes 3 zeros): 806,335.

mcqs.question: Which represents 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 in exponential form?
mcqs.explanation: 10 multiplied by itself 4 times is written with base 10 and exponent 4: 10⁴.

mcqs.question: Zoey wrote 10⁴ = 40. Which statement explains her error?
options: She multiplied the base 10 by the exponent 4 instead of multiplying 10 by itself 4 times.

mcqs.question: Estimate the product of 69 × 63 by rounding to the nearest ten.
mcqs.explanation: 69 rounds to 70 and 63 rounds to 60. Then 70 × 60 = 4,200.

mcqs.question: An airplane flies 482 miles per hour. Estimate how far it travels in 19 hours using rounding.
mcqs.explanation: Round 482 to 500 and 19 to 20. Then 500 × 20 = 10,000 miles.

1.tag: Alternative Practice 1.A • Comparing Digit Values in Multi-Digit Numbers
1.q:
Rialto, California had a population of $99,171$.
How do the values of the two $9$s in the ten-thousands place and thousands place compare?

steps.text: The $9$ in the ten-thousands place has a value of $90,000$. The $9$ in the thousands place has a value of $9,000$.
Since $90,000 = 10 \times 9,000$, the $9$ in the ten-thousands place is $10$ times the value of the $9$ in the thousands place.

1.ans: The $9$ in ten-thousands is $10$ times the value of the $9$ in thousands ($90,000 = 10 \times 9,000$).

1.tag: Alternative Practice 1.B • Converting Expanded Form to Standard and Word Form
1.q:
Write the given number in standard form and word form:
$$700,000 + 40,000 + 3,000 + 200 + 80 + 9$$

steps.text: Align by place value: $7$ hundred-thousands, $4$ ten-thousands, $3$ thousands, $2$ hundreds, $8$ tens, $9$ ones $= 743,289$.
Read period by period: "Seven hundred forty-three thousand, two hundred eighty-nine".

1.ans: Standard: $743,289$  |  Word: Seven hundred forty-three thousand, two hundred eighty-nine

1.tag: Alternative Practice 1.C • Expanded Form with Seven-Digit Numbers
1.q:
Write $5,248,319$ in expanded form:
Show the sum of the values of all digits in their respective places.

steps.text: $5$ millions $= 5,000,000$; $2$ hundred-thousands $= 200,000$; $4$ ten-thousands $= 40,000$; $8$ thousands $= 8,000$; $3$ hundreds $= 300$; $1$ ten $= 10$; $9$ ones $= 9$.

2.tag: Alternative Practice 2.A • Word-Unit Place Value Equivalence
2.q:
Complete the place value equivalence:
(a) $60\text{ thousands} = \dots\text{ hundreds}$
(b) $300\text{ tens} = \dots\text{ thousands}$

2.tag: Alternative Practice 2.B • Space Distance Multiplied by 10
2.q:
The distance from Earth to the Sun is approximately $93,000,000$ miles.
A space mission travels $10$ times this distance into the outer solar system. What is the total distance traveled?

steps.text: $93,000,000 \times 10$. Each digit shifts one place to the left, increasing in value by a factor of 10.

2.tag: Alternative Practice 2.C • Division by 10 & Rightward Shifts
2.q:
Find the quotient and describe the digit shift:
$$4,500,000 \div 10$$

steps.text: Dividing by $10$ shifts every digit one place to the right, reducing each digit's value to $\frac{1}{10}$ of its original value.

2.ans: $450,000$ (Digits shift 1 place right, decreasing by a factor of 10)

3.tag: Alternative Practice 3.A • Repeated Factors to Exponential Form
3.q:
Write each expression in exponential form and find its value:
(a) $10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10$
(b) $10 \times 10 \times 10$

steps.text: The base is $10$. It is multiplied by itself $5$ times. Form: $10^5 = 100,000$.
The base is $10$. It is multiplied by itself $3$ times. Form: $10^3 = 1,000$.

3.tag: Alternative Practice 3.B • Error Analysis in Exponents
3.q:
Zoey wrote: "$10^4 = 40$".
Explain Zoey's mistake and write the correct standard form.

steps.text: Zoey multiplied the base by the exponent ($10 \times 4 = 40$). An exponent does not mean multiplication by the exponent; it indicates repeated multiplication of the base.

3.ans: Zoey multiplied base by exponent ($10 \times 4 = 40$). The correct value is $10^4 = 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 = 10,000$.

3.q:
A satellite has a mass of $4 \times 10^4\text{ kg}$.
Write this mass in standard form and word form.
3.ans: Standard form: $40,000\text{ kg}$  |  Word form: Forty thousand kilograms

4.tag: Alternative Practice 4.A • Multi-Digit Multiplication with Powers of 10
4.q:
Find the product for each expression:
(a) $34 \times 10^2$
(b) $18 \times 10^4$

Find the missing exponent $n$ to make the statement true:
$$6 \times 10^n = 600,000$$

steps.text: In $600,000$, there are $5$ zeros following the non-zero digit $6$.

5.tag: Alternative Practice 5.A • Airplane Travel Distance Estimation
5.q:
An airplane flies at an average speed of $482$ miles per hour.
Estimate how far it travels in $19$ hours using rounding to the highest place value.

steps.text: Round $482$ to nearest hundred: $500$. Round $19$ to nearest ten: $20$.

5.tag: Alternative Practice 5.B • Cafeteria Table Cost Estimation
5.q:
A school purchases $28$ cafeteria tables. Each table costs $\$315$.
Estimate the total cost using compatible numbers.

steps.text: Choose friendly numbers close to the actual values: $315 \to 300$, and $28 \to 30$.

5.q:
Venus takes $225$ Earth days to complete one orbit around the Sun.
Estimate how many Earth days it takes Venus to complete $16$ full orbits using compatible numbers or rounding.

steps.text: Notice $225 \approx 250$ and $16$ is a multiple of $4$: $250 \times 16 = 4,000\text{ days}$.
